sources.title: Property and economy
sources.verified_claim: Enfield describes strategic management of a council asset portfolio exceeding £1bn and links property, economic development and regeneration opportunities; council asset strategy does not establish development potential for the sample parcel.

sources.title: Evidence base
sources.verified_claim: Enfield's planning evidence base states the emerging Local Plan seeks 304,000 square metres of industrial floorspace and 40,000 square metres of town-centre office space by 2041, supported by employment-land evidence; borough targets are not parcel allocations.

sources.title: Havering Works: Employment and Skills advice
sources.verified_claim: Havering Works provides employment, training and skills support for residents; service availability can help connect people to growth opportunities but does not guarantee jobs or development at a sample parcel.

sources.title: Local business support
sources.verified_claim: Havering Works states its employer support aims to help residents benefit from opportunities arising from local developments through recruitment and skills pathways; employment support is not evidence that a particular development will proceed.

sources.title: Workspace
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth states it protects and grows workspace through the Lambeth Works programme, council assets, external funding and Section 106 delivery, alongside an Affordable Workspace Policy; programme activity does not prove demand or delivery on a sample parcel.

sources.title: Supplementary Planning Documents (SPDs)
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth records adoption of its Affordable Workspace SPD on 28 April 2022 to guide implementation of Local Plan Policy ED2 for larger office developments in defined parts of the borough; the SPD is guidance, not parcel development evidence.

sources.title: London Growth Plan
sources.verified_claim: The London Growth Plan aims to raise productivity and create more good jobs while linking housing, infrastructure, skills and transport investment; strategic targets and programmes are not site-specific demand or funding awards.

sources.title: 4. Growing London's economy in a way that benefits all
sources.verified_claim: The July 2026 Draft London Plan economy chapter includes draft policies on employment space, industrial land, data centres, culture and sector growth; draft status is explicit and is not treated as adopted parcel policy.
